title: Turn any topic into a short audio course with sources
summary: Assaf Kipnis built Claudemy, a Claude Code skill that reads 20-40 web pages per topic; the author says a 12-lesson course yields about 25 minutes of two-voice audio.
agent_role: The agent maps sub-topics, researches and reads sources with reader agents, merges themes, plans and writes lessons, and generates audio. The human reviews one sample lesson before the rest are made.
outcome: The author says a 12-lesson course takes one long Claude Code session and yields about 25 minutes of audio.
what_they_did: Assaf Kipnis built Claudemy, an add-on skill for Claude Code. You ask it to "teach me [topic]". It splits the topic into smaller parts and reads 20–40 web pages, no more than 3 from any one site. Helper agents take notes with sources. The skill groups the notes into themes and counts how many sources agree. It plans about 12 two-minute lessons and makes one sample. Then it waits for your reaction before writing and recording the rest. Voices come from ElevenLabs or free Mac voices.
how_it_went: The author says a 12-lesson course takes one long Claude Code session. It produces about 25 minutes of audio. Each lesson comes with a summary card, and the course comes with a playbook.
worth_knowing: A checker rejects any lesson that cites a page the research didn't actually read. Without a paid ElevenLabs key, it uses plainer Mac voices. Health, legal and money topics get a note that advice depends on your situation.
prompt: Teach me [topic] at a [beginner/intermediate] level. Research 20–40 web pages from practitioners, official docs, research summaries and a few dissenting views, with no more than 3 from any one site. Take cited notes, group them into themes, and show how many sources agree on each point and where they disagree. Plan about 12 two-minute lessons, foundations first. Write one sample lesson as a two-host script with a three-line summary, one thing to try and source links, then wait for my feedback before writing the rest. Only cite pages you actually read.

curation.rationale: The multi-step research-to-audio workflow is clear and reproducible, with source checks and agent roles spelled out. However, the README shows no specific course built or result achieved, so it is borderline; the score includes a small education boost.
